notes: Telangana's KNRUHS counsels the Competent Authority Quota (these lines) in phases: first, second, mop-up, an additional mop-up, then a stray vacancy phase. Each phase has its own notice. Management Quota seats need a separate registration.

r1.title: First phase
chips: Skip it: out of every later phase
Don't join: out of later rounds
who: Candidates on the final merit list whose uploaded certificates were provisionally verified (the final check is at the college, and a discrepancy cancels the allotment). Service candidates also choose service-quota seats; minority-college seats go to Muslim minority candidates only.
If you don't use web options in this phase, you can't in any later phase.
opts: Pay the University fee of Rs 29,600 to download the allotment order, then report with all original certificates and the bonds and pay the tuition fee at the college. The college keeps your originals until you complete the course (the prospectus makes this subject to the two bonds); the notice says they're returned if you discontinue. Fees paid aren't refunded.
The University fee and other fees once paid shall not be refunded under any circumstances.
The admission is cancelled, and you can't use web options in any later round. No money penalty is stated.

IMPORANT NOTE: Candidates are informed that if they exercise web- options for a seat and allotted a PG seat as per their choice in the web- counseling and if they do not join the course at the allotted college, they will not be eligible for exercising web- options for subsequent rounds of counseling.
gaps: any rule for candidates holding an all-India, deemed or central seat in the first or second phase.

r2.title: Second phase
chips: Free exit: no penalty, but out
who: Candidates who used web options in the first phase, joiners still on the course included, and candidates added to the merit list later. Not those allotted in the first phase who didn't report, or joined and discontinued.
opts: Your first-phase seat is cancelled automatically and given to someone else. Get relieved from the first college, collect your originals and fees, and join the new one by the last date.

If a PG seat is allotted in this phase of counseling as per web options exercised by the candidate, the seat allotted in 1st phase of counseling will be automatically cancelled and allotted to the other candidate.
Your first-phase seat was cancelled when this one was allotted, so you have neither seat, and you can't take part in any further phase.
Candidates who do not join the course at the allotted college in this phase of counseling are not eligible for further phases of counseling.

Candidates admitted up to this phase could leave without penalty until 4 PM on 23.01.2026, and in-service candidates kept that date. For non-service candidates it was extended five times, the last time to 4 PM on 09.02.2026, after MCC's Round 3 allotments of 06.02.2026. You apply to the college Principal, who returns the originals, bonds and tuition fee, but you then can't take part in any further Competent Authority Quota round.
However, the candidates are informed that they will not be eligible for further rounds of Competent Authority Quota counseling for PG Medical courses once they discontinue the course.
fe: p.1; fex: p.1; fexl: p.1
gaps: whether a Competent Authority Quota joiner could move to a Management Quota seat between phases: not found in the documents we hold.

r3.title: Mop-up
who: Non-service candidates on the final merit list of 11-02-2026 who used web options in the first phase. Those allotted earlier who didn't report, or discontinued, can't; joiners still on the course can, to slide.

Everyone who joined an all-India seat up to MCC's third round is weeded out before allotment, and those admitted in MCC's Round 3 are told not to take part. For the additional mop-up, anyone on MCC's admitted list after its Round 3 isn't eligible.

In-service candidates had a mop-up of their own first: web options were notified on 28.01.2026, and a High Court order of 03.02.2026 opened a separate window, from 1 PM on 07.02.2026 to 1 PM on 08.02.2026, for the candidates in that court case only. Service seats left over go to the non-service seats: the mop-up notice added those not taken up by 4 PM on 11.02.2026, though in-service reporting was then extended to 4 PM on 12.02.2026.
misp: p.1; mop: p.2; misr: p.1
In 2025-26 mop-up allottees had to report by 1 PM on 19.02.2026 (extended from 5 PM on 18.02.2026).
opts: Your earlier seat is cancelled automatically. Get relieved from the earlier college, collect the custodian certificate and fees, and join by the last date.

If PG seat is allotted in this phase of counseling as per web options exercised by the candidate, the seat allotted in previous phase of counseling will be automatically cancelled and allotted to the other candidate.
The admission is cancelled, you pay a penalty of Rs 50 lakh, and you're barred from PG admission under KNRUHS for 3 years.

If the candidate does not fulfill the above criteria to complete the admission process within the specified date, the admission will be cancelled automatically and the candidate will be considered as being part of seat blocking and candidate has to pay penalty of Rs. 50 lakhs and also debarred for 3 years for PG Medical admission under KNRUHS.
You can't take part in the Management Quota mop-up or in either stray phase.

Candidates who were allotted seats in this phase of counselling are not eligible to exercise web-options in Mop-Up Phase of counselling under Management Quota and stray vacancy phase of counselling under Competent Authority Quota and Management Quota for the AY 2025-26.

A second mop-up, for vacant non-service and newly added seats, ran on 19-20 February 2026. Joiners still on their course could slide again; anyone on MCC's admitted list after its Round 3 couldn't take part. Not joining costs Rs 50,00,000 and a 3-year bar, and the list of those admitted and allotted after it went to MCC to keep them out of MCC's stray round.

If a candidate is allotted a seat in this phase of counselling and does not join the course, he will be liable for payment of penalty of Rs. 50,00,000/- (Rupees Fifty Lakhs only) to KNRUHS and also shall be debarred for 3 years from PG Medical admissions under KNRUHS.
gaps: the in-service mop-up rules: the University's in-service mop-up notice of 28-01-2026 is no longer on its site.
whether in-service seats left after the extended reporting deadline (4 PM on 12.02.2026) went into this phase: the notices don't say.
how the first-phase condition applies to candidates who registered only after the cut-off was lowered in January 2026: the mop-up notices repeat it and don't say.

stray.title: Stray vacancy phase
chips: Only if never allotted a CQ seat
who: Candidates on the final merit list of 11-02-2026 who used web options in the first phase. Anyone allotted a Competent Authority Quota seat in an earlier phase is barred, whether they joined, didn't join or discontinued.

Not eligible: those admitted under Management Quota or allotted in its mop-up, and those on MCC's admitted list up to its mop-up round or allotted in its stray round. Anyone admitted to a PG seat anywhere in India is advised not to take part, as it amounts to seat blocking; if the University notices it at any stage, the admission is cancelled automatically and the candidate is liable for punishment under the law.
opts: Pay the University fee of Rs 29,600 to download the allotment letter, then report with all originals and bonds and pay the tuition fee by the last date.
Allotted Candidates have to pay University fee of Rs.29,600/- by way of online payment gate-way and download the allotment letter.
You pay a penalty of Rs 50,00,000 to KNRUHS and are barred from PG admission under KNRUHS for 3 years.

If a candidate is allotted a seat in this phase of counselling and does not join the course, he will be liable for payment of penalty of Rs. 50,00,000/- (Rupees Fifty Lakhs only) to KNRUHS and also shall be debarred for 3 years from PG Medical admissions under KNRUHS.
gaps: how the first-phase condition applies to candidates who registered only after the cut-off was lowered in January 2026: the notices don't say.

after.title: Leaving the course
chips: After free exit: Rs 50 lakh + 3-year bar
opts: After the last free-exit date (in 2025-26, 4 PM on 23.01.2026 for in-service candidates and, after extensions, 4 PM on 09.02.2026 for non-service candidates) you aren't permitted to withdraw. Discontinuing then costs Rs 50,00,000 and a 3-year bar from PG counselling under KNRUHS; the free-exit notice to those admitted up to the second phase adds the tuition fee for the whole course.

Candidates are informed that if they discontinue the course after 04.00 P.M on 23.01.2026 onwards, penalty clause will be applicable with payment of tuition fee for the entire course and Rs.50,00,000/- (Rupees Fifty Lakh Only) of Bond amount and are debarred from admission into PG Medical courses under KNRUHS for 3 years.

Every candidate, in-service too, signs a bond to complete the course, or pay Rs 50,00,000 to KNRUHS and refund the stipend or salary received.

All the candidates including In-service candidates joining into the Post Graduate degree, diploma courses shall execute bond on a non-judicial stamp paper of Rs. 100/- as prescribed in Annexure-II to the effect that he / she shall complete the prescribed period of training or in default to pay Rs.50,00,000/- (Rupees Fifty Lakhs only) to the KNRUHS and shall refund the amount received as stipend/salary upto that date to the Government.
Serve the Government of Telangana for one year, if necessary, in government institutions; the bond signed at admission is Rs 20,00,000 for a degree and Rs 10,00,000 for a diploma.

All Postgraduates (excluding in-service candidates) shall serve the Government of Telangana, if necessary, in Government institutions for a period of one year as per the orders of the Telangana State Government.
